name: CHAI
notice: Checklist items are this project's paraphrased summaries organized around the CHAI six-stage lifecycle and five principles. They are not the official CHAI Responsible AI Checklist text.

sections.title: Define the problem & plan
sections.blurb: Agree on the clinical or operational problem, confirm AI is the right tool, and name who is accountable before anything is built or bought.

items.text: Problem statement and target outcome agreed with clinical and operational stakeholders
Current-state or root-cause analysis shows AI is an appropriate intervention, not just a possible one
Success measures and a baseline to compare against are defined
Affected patient populations identified, including groups at risk of being underserved or harmed
Potential harms and failure modes listed, with severity and likelihood
Accountable owner, governance body, and decision rights named
Data needs, privacy, consent, and regulatory constraints scoped

sections.title: Design the AI system
sections.blurb: Specify how the system fits into care: who uses it, where in the workflow, what it outputs, and what happens when it is wrong.

items.text: End users took part in workflow and interface design
Intended use, users, and care setting documented, with out-of-scope uses listed
Subgroups and fairness criteria for evaluation pre-specified
Decision thresholds defined and clinically justified
Human oversight and override path designed into the workflow
Pathway for reporting safety issues and harms drafted, naming who reports to whom
Threat model, access controls, and data flows designed

sections.title: Engineer the AI solution
sections.blurb: Build or configure the model with traceable data and documented choices, so the assessment stage has something it can verify.

items.text: Data provenance and known data limitations documented
Demographic and socio-demographic make-up of development data characterized
Bias mitigation approach chosen and documented
Data quality checks and handling of missing data documented
Version control in place for datasets, code, and model artifacts
De-identification or other privacy-enhancing techniques applied where appropriate
People responsible for monitoring data and model behavior designated

sections.title: Assess
sections.blurb: Validate the solution locally before patients are exposed to it. Record key metrics below; they flow into the model card.

items.text: Performance validated on local data representative of the deployment population
Performance compared across demographic subgroups, with gaps explained
Calibration checked, not only discrimination
Silent (shadow) evaluation run in the live environment
Installation qualification completed, where applicable
Explanations of outputs are suited to the intended users
Security review or vendor security assessment completed
Safety reporting pathway updated with what assessment revealed

sections.title: Pilot
sections.blurb: Run a small, time-boxed pilot to learn whether the solution helps in real care, for whom, and at what cost to staff.

items.text: Pilot scope, sites, duration, and stop rules defined
Usability and workflow fit assessed with frontline users
Real-world effect on outcomes or process measured against baseline
Pilot results checked for differences across patient groups
Adverse events and near misses tracked and reviewed
Users trained, and the approach to patient disclosure decided

sections.title: Deploy & monitor
sections.blurb: Scale up with monitoring, change control, and a plan for when to retrain or retire.

items.text: Performance and drift monitoring live, with alert thresholds and an owner
Subgroup performance monitored on an ongoing basis
Audit schedule and change control set, with a revised model card for each version
Incident response, rollback, and retirement criteria documented
Access reviews and security patching scheduled
Value to patients and staff re-evaluated periodically

gates.title: Checkpoint A
gates.question: Approve moving to design?
gates.help: Is the problem worth solving with AI, and is the plan sound enough to start design?

gates.title: Checkpoint B
gates.question: Approve a pilot?
gates.help: Has local assessment shown the solution is safe, effective, and fair enough to expose a small group of patients to it?

gates.title: Checkpoint C
gates.question: Approve deployment at scale?
gates.help: Did the pilot show real benefit without unacceptable harm or disparity?

gates.title: Checkpoint D
gates.question: Periodic review decision
gates.help: Based on monitoring, should the solution continue as is, change, or be retired? Record a new review each cycle; the next due date is set from it.
